 Fired Healey Aide Indicted for Second Wire Fraud After Allegedly Using SNAP for Disney Trip While Facing Cocaine Charges 
 Also available in Português / Español 
 Share 
 Advertisement 
 A federal grand jury has indicted former Massachusetts official Lamar Cook on a second count of wire fraud tied to his alleged scheme to obtain SNAP benefits while free on pretrial release in a separate state drug and firearm case.
 Cook, 46, of Springfield, previously faced a federal criminal complaint charging him with one count of SNAP fraud and one count of wire fraud after his October arrest . The new indictment, returned Wednesday, treats two electronic transmissions of his April 6, 2026, benefits application as separate offenses: one involving a server in Virginia and another involving a service provider in Wisconsin. He is scheduled for arraignment on the added charge Monday in federal court in Boston.
 Prosecutors allege Cook submitted an online application claiming zero income, less than $100 in the bank, and a household limited to himself and a minor child. Court records show his account held more than $8,800 that day. He also allegedly omitted that his fiancée, a Springfield Public Schools employee earning over $80,000 annually, and her mother lived with him. Additional inflows included roughly $12,000 in Zelle transfers from his mother after she won approximately $1 million in the Massachusetts Lottery, a tax refund, and a post-termination vacation payout.
 Massachusetts State Police photo. 
 Cook had worked as Western Massachusetts Deputy Director in Governor Maura Healey’s office since 2023, with an annual salary around $130,227. He was terminated in October 2025 after being detained at the Springfield State Office building and charged by the Hampden District Attorney’s Office. State authorities accused him of involvement in cocaine trafficking, including the interception of a package containing about 8 kilograms of the drug at the office building where he worked, with additional parcels linked to Hotel UMass in Amherst. Related state charges include trafficking more than 200 grams of cocaine, conspiracy, and firearm offenses. Cook has pleaded not guilty to the state charges.
 Advertisement 
 While on pretrial release, Cook received about $546 per month in SNAP benefits. Records indicate approximately $3,274 in benefits were spent between early April and mid-October 2026 at Massachusetts retailers and during a July trip to Florida. Reporting noted use of his EBT card near Walt Disney World.
 U.S. Attorney Leah B. Foley previously described the alleged SNAP conduct as “simply egregious,” noting that benefits are meant for struggling families. Officials from the USDA and HHS have characterized the case as a betrayal of public trust.
 Each wire fraud count carries a potential sentence of up to 20 years in prison. The SNAP fraud charge carries up to five years. The state drug and firearm case remains pending in Hampden County Superior Court. After the initial federal charges, a state judge revoked Cook’s bail for 90 days. Cook is presumed innocent of all charges until proven guilty.
